items.name: ANNA_CHROME_EXECUTABLE / ANNA_CHROME_VERSION
items.summary: Absolute path + four-part version of the platform Chrome for Testing, resolved by the Agent — never guess `chromium-<rev>` directory names. `ANNA_CHROME_PROVIDER` is always `playwright-cft`.

wire.ANNA_CHROME_EXECUTABLE: absolute path, e.g. `/ms-playwright/chromium-1200/chrome-linux/chrome` (cloud) · `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1200/chrome-mac-arm64/Google Chrome for Testing.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome for Testing` (macOS)
wire.semantics: set only when Chrome is ready to run; absent (never empty) means not available on this Agent

limitations: Paths are readable + executable by your process but the directories are **shared platform state** — never write into them.
`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` may also be visible; it is an implementation detail, **not** part of the contract, and its layout belongs to Playwright.
Set `"puppeteer": { "skipDownload": true }` in `package.json` (or `PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1` in CI) so your build never pulls its own Chrome.
Keep concurrent Chrome instances ≤ 3–4 on Cloud Agents (limited microVM memory).
Compare **majors only** — the build follows the platform Playwright pin and changes with Matrix releases.

items.name: ANNA_NODE_EXECUTABLE / ANNA_NODE_VERSION
items.summary: Absolute path + full version of the shared Node 22 LTS. Lets a binary-distributed Node tool ship a 2-line shell shim instead of an embedded Node (~120 MiB saved).

wire.provisioning: baked into Cloud Agent images; on desktop Agents installed once from the agent console ("Platform" row, ~30 MiB) — a `runtime.requires` declaration never installs anything
wire.semantics: set only when Node is ready to run; absent (never empty) means not available on this Agent

limitations: Pinned to the **Node 22 LTS line** on every channel; a major switch goes through a separate design review and is announced in advance.
No rollbacks — if your tool hard-depends on an exact Node build, bundle your own runtime and set `runtime.fallback: "bundled"`.
Shell / `.cmd` shims are regular entrypoints of the multi-file binary pipeline — see Binary distribution.

items.name: ANNA_RUNTIME_PROFILE / ANNA_AGENT_VERSION / ANNA_RUNTIMES_JSON
items.summary: Where you run, the Matrix Agent version for capability gating, and a compact JSON summary of the whole contract.

wire.ANNA_RUNTIMES_JSON: `{"profile": …, "chrome": {"executable", "version", "provider"}, "node": {"executable", "version"}}` — same facts as the individual variables

limitations: Older Agents that predate the contract set **none** of these variables — the demo app's `legacy-scan` fallback shows how to degrade.
The contract is identical across all channels; branch on `ANNA_RUNTIME_PROFILE` only for genuinely platform-specific behaviour (e.g. `--no-sandbox` on cloud).

items.name: runtime.requires
items.since: Matrix Agent runtime contract (forum #490) · tools only
items.summary: Declare semver ranges for `node` / `chrome` so a missing runtime fails at **install time** with a structured `runtime_missing` error instead of crashing at invoke time.

params.name: requires.node
params.desc: Range the shared Node must satisfy. Operators `>` `>=` `<` `<=` `=` `^` `~`, space = AND, `||` = OR. Anything else is rejected at publish time.

params.name: requires.chrome
params.desc: Range for the platform Chrome. Only the **major** is compared — never pin an exact build like `146.0.7680.153`.

params.name: fallback
params.desc: `bundled` means your package ships its own runtime and still runs when the platform one is missing — the precheck then only warns.

returns.desc: On an unmet requirement the install fails with `reason_code: "runtime_missing"` and a `missing_runtimes` map such as `{"node": "required >=22 <23, found none"}`.

limitations: The precheck is a **pure check** — a declaration never installs anything. Cloud Agents have the shared Node baked in; desktop users install it once from the agent console ("Platform" row) and retry the app install.
Older Agents that predate the contract ignore the block (no precheck, no crash) — fully backwards compatible.
Applies to `executa_type: "tool"` packages.

items.name: GET /api/v1/platform/runtimes
items.summary: Public, unauthenticated, cacheable version matrix per release channel — current versions plus the announced next with `effective_from`. Feeds the generated blocks on the docs page and `anna-app doctor`.

returns.desc: `{schema: 1, generated_at, policy: {chrome, node}, channels: {"cloud-linux" | "desktop-macos" | "desktop-windows": {current: {agent_version, components: {chrome: {version}, node: {version}}} | null, next: {agent_version?, effective_from?, components?} | null}}}`. `current: null` means the channel has not published a matrix yet.

items.example:
curl -sS -H 'Accept: application/json' https://anna.partners/api/v1/platform/runtimes | jq '.channels["cloud-linux"]'
# or, with the CLI:
anna-app doctor
limitations: Planning-time truth only — at run time trust your own process env (`ANNA_CHROME_VERSION` / `ANNA_NODE_VERSION`); desktop users may lag several Matrix versions behind.
Version matrix and *Upcoming* blocks on the docs page are regenerated from this endpoint by `matrix-nexus/scripts/export_platform_runtimes.py` — do not edit them by hand.

items.name: Cloud (linux-x86_64)
limitations: **Chrome policy** — Follows the Matrix Playwright pin. Major bumps are announced >= 14 days ahead; a given major stays available across >= 2 Matrix minor releases. Compare major only.
**Node.js policy** — Pinned to the Node 22 LTS line across all channels. Major switches go through a separate design review and are announced in advance.
Planning-time truth only — the run-time truth is your own process env (`ANNA_CHROME_VERSION` / `ANNA_NODE_VERSION`); desktop users may lag several Matrix versions behind this matrix.
